newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf 1996 operating seen up by over 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Elf 1996 operating seen up by over 25 pct.

text.p: The 1996 operating profit of oil group Elf-Aquitaine, due to be announced on Wednesday, should be more than 25 percent higher than the 1995 figures, according to a source close to the company.

This rise from the 1995 figure of 15.5 billion francs is mainly due to the upstream activities which benefited from the rise of Brent and the dollar, the source added, based the estimate on recent preliminary figures.
A spokeswoman for Elf had no comment on the figures.
Elf said in mid-December that its current net attributable profit for 1996 would be between 7.3 and 7.5 billion francs, against 5.3 billion in 1995.

The operating result for upstream activities should be some 14 billion francs in 1996 from eight billion in 1995. This was helped by the price of oil -- each dollar increase boosts the operating figure by 1.5 billion francs. The average price of Brent rose to $20.9 per barrel from $17 in 1995.

The operating result of downstream activities was slightly positive in 1996 against nil in 1995. Health activities, mainly in Sanofi, had an increase in operating income of 10 percent compared to the 2.5 billion francs of 1995.
In chemicals the operating income is down in line with sales which were down to 53.26 billion francs from 54.86 billion.
Group investments were down by two billion francs from 26 billion in 1995 while the company made asset sales to the tune of between three and four billion francs.
The source said that Elf was using a Brent price of $16.5 per barrel and a dollar at 5.20 francs for its planning for the 1997-2000 period.
Spot Brent was trading at around $20 on Monday and the franc was at 5.65 to the dollar.
